metadata.note: Three railroads that made Shreveport, LA a rail crossroads: the Kansas City Southern's north-south trunk and its Southern Belle flagship, the Texas & Pacific's route southeast to New Orleans, and the Vicksburg, Shreveport & Pacific running east to the Mississippi. Shreveport had four separate passenger terminals at its peak, and has had no passenger service since the Southern Belle ended in 1969 - Amtrak's Texas Eagle passes about 60km west via Marshall, TX without serving it. Geometry south and east of Shreveport is now traced from real OpenStreetMap track (Overpass API + shortest-path graph search), following the surviving corridors: CPKC's New Orleans Subdivision for the KCS route, Union Pacific's ex-Missouri Pacific subdivisions for the T&P, and CPKC's Vicksburg Subdivision for the VS&P. The KCS leg north of Shreveport toward Kansas City is still hand-placed town waypoints, as it fell outside the traced area. CORRECTION (2026-08-19): an earlier version of this file said the KCS and T&P were competing parallel routes all the way to New Orleans. They were separate railroads between Shreveport and Baton Rouge, but from 1940 - when the new Mississippi River bridge at Baton Rouge opened - KCS's Southern Belle and Flying Crow were diverted onto Texas & Pacific rails for the Baton Rouge-New Orleans leg, so south of Baton Rouge the two features intentionally share identical geometry because they were the same physical track. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Arthur Stilwell's Kansas City, Pittsburg & Gulf reached the Gulf at Port Arthur in 1897, reorganized as the Kansas City Southern Railway in 1900 - a north-south trunk cutting against the era's east-west grain, with Shreveport a key point on it. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Through Shreveport-New Orleans passenger service was inaugurated Apr 14 1907. KCS owned Shreveport Union Station; the city was busy enough that it had four separate passenger terminals rather than one. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: KCS acquired the Louisiana & Arkansas Railway Oct 20 1939, which had itself absorbed the Louisiana Railway & Navigation Company in 1929 - the LR&N having been organized May 9 1903 and built its own 303.966-mile main line from New Orleans via Baton Rouge and Alexandria to Shreveport. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Southern Belle, KCS's flagship, was inaugurated Sept 2 1940 running Kansas City-New Orleans via Joplin, Texarkana, Shreveport, Alexandria and Baton Rouge - 868.1 miles daily in about 21.5 hours. Note it did NOT use KCS-owned rail the whole way: when the new Mississippi River bridge at Baton Rouge opened in 1940, the Southern Belle and the Flying Crow were diverted onto Texas & Pacific track for the Baton Rouge-New Orleans leg, so south of Baton Rouge this line and the T&P line here are the same physical railroad, not parallel ones. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: After the US Postal Service cancelled railway mail contracts in 1967-68 and ridership fell, the Southern Belle (trains 1 and 2) made its last run Nov 2 1969 - a year and a half before Amtrak, which never served Shreveport. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

properties.line: Texas and Pacific: Shreveport – New Orleans
properties.speed_source: estimated/blended across the line's history; unsourced

segments.note: The Texas & Pacific assembled several Louisiana lines and completed a through route from Shreveport to New Orleans on Sept 12 1882. From 1940 it also carried KCS's Southern Belle and Flying Crow between Baton Rouge and New Orleans, so that portion is shared track rather than a competing parallel route. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
